data.name: StackTip
data.value: Stack every window on the last one used, at its place and size.

data.name: SideBySideTip
data.value: Lay two windows side by side, each on one half of the screen. The active window goes to the right.

data.name: GridTip
data.value: Lay the windows out in a grid, each on a quarter of the screen, in the order of the list. Beyond four, the next ones stack on the last cell.

data.name: ArrangeMenuTip
data.value: Arrange the windows: stack, side by side or grid

data.name: GuidesTip
data.value: Open the papycha.fr guides (quests, dungeons, paths…), which stay above the game windows.

data.name: QuitTip
data.value: Close the application and the game windows

data.name: PlaceWindowsTip
data.value: Click a cell to gather every window at that spot on the screen. It is also the corner where windows with no remembered place open.

data.name: WindowSizeTip
data.value: As a share of the screen, not in pixels: the same look on every screen. Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+5 give five sizes.

data.name: QualityLowTip
data.value: 720 at most, 30 frames per second, reduced bitrate, phone polled less often. For modest devices or many accounts.

data.name: QualityMediumTip
data.value: 1080 at most, 30 frames per second. Suits most machines.

data.name: QualityElevatedTip
data.value: 1080 at most, 60 frames per second instead of 30. For the account you play, the others staying at Medium.

data.name: QualityMaximumTip
data.value: Image at 1440 at most, 60 frames per second. Hard on the phone: keep it for a recent device, and over Wi-Fi for a network that keeps up.

data.name: QualityCustomTip
data.value: Set the resolution, frame rate, image detail and codec yourself. For those who know what they want.

data.name: QualityValues
data.value: {0}p max · {1} fps · about {2} Mb/s per window

data.name: MaxResolutionTip
data.value: A ceiling: the actual resolution follows the window's size and can be lower.

data.name: ImageDetailTip
data.value: Bits per pixel and per frame. The bitrate follows the window's size, for an image as fine small as large.

data.name: VideoCodecTip
data.value: AV1 and VP8 are not offered: on an ordinary phone they have no hardware encoder, and encoding them in software costs far more than they give back.

data.name: BitsPerPixelTip
data.value: Bits given to each pixel of each frame. About 0.10 gives good-quality H.264.

data.name: BitrateTip
data.value: What the phone sends over Wi-Fi. On Wi-Fi 4 at 2.4 GHz, count on sixty megabits at most.

data.name: ResolutionAdviceTip
data.value: The resolution follows the windows' size. 1440 instead of 1080 only shows on a window over 1800 pixels high, for far more bitrate.

data.name: GameDistanceTip
data.value: More or less ground in view, at the same window size. Acts on the game screen's density, not on the image's detail.

data.name: ZoomVeryFarTip
data.value: The most ground it is possible to show. The game interface becomes small: on a modest window it will be at the edge of legible.

data.name: ZoomFarTip
data.value: A lot of ground visible, the game interface small. Handy to follow several accounts at a glance, less comfortable to aim.

data.name: ZoomSlightlyFarTip
data.value: A little more ground than normal, the game interface a little smaller.

data.name: ZoomNormalTip
data.value: The original setting, that of a 1080 pixel display at 240 dpi.

data.name: ZoomCloseTip
data.value: The least ground, the largest game interface: for a small window. Above 2300 pixels high, it nearly matches the previous step.

data.name: ReopenNotice
data.value: Open windows reopen to take the change.

data.name: PhoneAudio
data.value: Phone sound sent back to the PC

data.name: PhoneAudioTip
data.value: Android sends the whole phone's sound, all accounts mixed: one window per phone carries it.

data.name: SharpImageTip
data.value: Renders the game at twice the window's size: coloured text, like red on grey, gets as sharp as white. More work for the phone and the PC, no more Wi-Fi: avoid on a modest device.

data.name: AutomaticUpdatesTip
data.value: The new version downloads in the background and installs when you quit. Unchecked, the application only says that a version exists.

data.name: StopAppOnClose
data.value: Close the game on the phone too

data.name: StopAppOnCloseTip
data.value: Closing a window also stops the game on the phone. Unticked, the game keeps running: the reopened window finds the character logged in, but it takes up the phone's memory.

data.name: TurnScreenOff
data.value: Turn the phone's screen off while playing

data.name: TurnScreenOffTip
data.value: The phone's screen turns off when a game window opens, and the game goes on on the PC: less heat, more battery. It comes back on when the last account closes. The line under the phone, or Ctrl+E, turns it off or on at any time.

data.name: AppPickerShowHelp
data.value: Ticked, it appears in the list and opens in its own window, like the game. Nothing is installed or copied on the phone.

data.name: AppPickerSystemApps
data.value: Also show the phone's own applications

data.name: AppPickerNotListed
data.value: Not found on the phone this time

data.name: AppPickerCloneHeader
data.value: Clone the game onto a new account

data.name: AppPickerCloneHelp
data.value: Creates a new Android profile on the phone, with its own copy of the game, for one more account. The game will ask again for its resources and the login.

data.name: RemoveAppTip
data.value: Remove from the list. The app stays on the phone, and the + button puts it back.

data.name: AppPickerLoadFailed
data.value: The phone's applications could not be read. Close this window and try again.

data.name: AppsStillOpen
data.value: Still open, so kept in the list: {0}. Close its window, then remove it.

data.name: PairDeviceTip
data.value: Once per phone, by cable or wireless. After that, it connects on its own.

data.name: ProfilesTip
data.value: Groups of accounts, with their positions and their settings, opened in one gesture.

data.name: NoProfilesYet
data.value: No team yet. Open your accounts, place their windows, then create one.

data.name: LaunchProfileTip
data.value: Open this team: its accounts open in place with its settings, the other windows close.

data.name: DeleteProfileTip
data.value: Delete this team. The accounts are not touched.

data.name: ProfileOpenExplained
data.value: Opening it later will close the game windows that are not part of it, then open its accounts where they stood, with these settings.

data.name: ProfileExistsQuestion
data.value: A team “{0}” already exists. Replace what it keeps with what is open now?

data.name: UpdateProfileTip
data.value: Replace what this team keeps with the accounts open now, their windows and the current settings.

data.name: UpdateProfileQuestion
data.value: Update the team “{0}” with what is open now?

data.name: UpdateProfileReplaces
data.value: What it kept until now will be replaced. Its name, its place in the list and its startup choice stay.

data.name: CreateProfileTip
data.value: Remember the open accounts, their positions and the current settings under a name.

data.name: LanguageTip
data.value: "Windows" follows the system's language, or English if it is not translated. Applies at the next startup.

data.name: LanguageRestart
data.value: The language changes at the next start.

data.name: FrenchLabelsNotice
data.value: Labels of a phone set to English. In another language, the menus stay in the same order.

data.name: PairCodeIntro
data.value: 1. On the phone: Wireless debugging › Pair device with pairing code. 2. It shows up here: type the six-digit code.

data.name: HelpTip
data.value: Where to find these settings on your phone

data.name: PairingCodeTip
data.value: The six-digit code shown on the device

data.name: PortTip
data.value: The number after ":" in "IP address & port", on the Wireless debugging screen.

data.name: TapSevenTimesPrefix
data.value: Tap seven times in a row on “

data.name: TapSevenTimesSuffix
data.value: ”. A message confirms that you are a developer.

data.name: CableSteps
data.value: Plug in the cable, then accept the request on the phone and tick “Always allow”. It then shows up in DT Hub on its own.

data.name: WirelessMenuPath
data.value: Wireless debugging › Pair device with pairing code

data.name: WirelessCodeShown
data.value: Type the six-digit code it shows into DT Hub. The PC and the phone must be on the same Wi-Fi, with Android 11 at least.

data.name: StaysOfflineSameBand
data.value: • The PC and the phone on the same Wi-Fi, not on the router's guest Wi-Fi.

data.name: StaysOfflinePrivate
data.value: • Windows: the network set to “Private” (Settings › Network & internet).

data.name: StaysOfflineFirewall
data.value: • Windows firewall: allow “Android Debug Bridge” on Private and Public.

data.name: StaysOfflineVpn
data.value: • Turn off the PC's VPN, if there is one.

data.name: StaysOfflineByHand
data.value: • As a last resort: “Type the address by hand”, in the pairing window.

data.name: AndroidOnly
data.value: Only Android devices will do. iOS allows neither opening an extra display nor installing the same application twice.

data.name: ShortcutsScopeNotice
data.value: They only act while a window of the application is active, so your other programs keep every key.

data.name: AddAccountTip
data.value: Show another application of this phone, or clone the game onto a new account.

data.name: ForgetDeviceTip
data.value: Forgets this phone on this PC: its windows close, its accounts and settings are erased. The phone is not touched. Asks for confirmation.

data.name: StopDeviceTip
data.value: Close every account of this phone. The other phones are not touched.

data.name: ForgetDeviceShortTip
data.value: Forgets this phone on this PC: its accounts and settings are erased. The phone is not touched. Asks for confirmation.

data.name: DragToReorderTip
data.value: Drag to change the order, even between two phones' accounts. It is also the keyboard cycling order.

data.name: LockWindowTip
data.value: Pins this window in place: stacking, side by side, resizing and keyboard cycling leave it alone. In the tab frame, one locked tab pins the whole frame.

data.name: PhoneFormat
data.value: Phone's ratio (if the game is shifted)

data.name: PhoneFormatTip
data.value: Leave unticked, unless the game shows shifted, cut or with a black band on one side (seen on a Galaxy Tab and an ultrawide screen). The game then takes the phone's format, with black bands around it if your screen differs. Applies at the next opening.

data.name: TabbedTip
data.value: Open this account in the tabbed frame. Click again to give it back its own free window.

data.name: RenameTip
data.value: Click to rename: this name becomes the game window's title.

data.name: OpenInstanceTip
data.value: Open this account. Its window comes back at its place and size.

data.name: RestartTip
data.value: Restarts the game without closing the window: useful if it froze. It comes back to the login screen, same place, same size.

data.name: CloseWindowTip
data.value: Closes this account's window. Nothing is deleted: the Play button reopens it in the same place. It will not reopen on its own at startup.

data.name: NoDeviceHelp
data.value: Plug in a USB cable, debugging on: the phone shows up on its own. Already paired over Wi-Fi? It comes back on its own on the network.

data.name: CheckReady
data.value: The phone answers. Everything is ready.

data.name: CheckNoDevice
data.value: No phone detected. Seeing it in Windows Photos is not enough: 1. Plug in a data cable. 2. Pick "File transfer" if the phone asks. 3. Turn on USB debugging. A phone already paired over Wi-Fi comes back on its own.

data.name: CheckWaitingAuthorization
data.value: The phone is there but has not authorised this PC yet. Unlock its screen and accept the debugging prompt.

data.name: CheckDriverRefused
data.value: The Windows USB driver refuses access to this device. Unplug it, plug it into another port, and accept the prompt on the phone.

data.name: CheckUsbUnreadable
data.value: A device is plugged in but Windows could not read its identity. The cable, the port or the connector is at fault, not the phone.

data.name: CheckUsbDriverMissing
data.value: A device is plugged in, but Windows has no driver for its debugging: 1. Download Google's USB driver (developer.android.com/studio/run/win-usb) and unzip it. 2. Device Manager › right-click the line with the yellow triangle › Update driver › Browse my computer › Let me pick from a list › Have Disk › android_winusb.inf › "Android ADB Interface". Confirm if Windows warns. 3. Unplug and plug the cable back in.

data.name: CheckUsbOther
data.value: A device is plugged in and Windows turned it away. The detail is in Device Manager.

data.name: CableHelpTitle
data.value: A plugged-in device Windows cannot read

data.name: CableHelpIntro
data.value: The phone charges but the PC does not see it: the cable or the port only carries power. Try, in this order:

data.name: CableHelpSteps
data.value: 1. Another cable: charger cables often have no data wires. 2. A USB port at the back of the PC. 3. "Restart" Windows: shutting down and back on is not enough. 4. Clean the phone's connector. 5. This phone on another PC, to know which one is at fault.

data.name: AdbShellUserAccessDenied
data.value: The phone refuses the PC access to this profile. Secure Folder: unlock it before launching. Otherwise, turn on "USB debugging (Security settings)" in the developer options.

data.name: ScrcpyDisplayTimeoutWithAudio
data.value: The phone did not open a virtual display in time. Try without sound first: on some tablets, turning it on is enough to stop the display from opening.

data.name: BrandSamsungWarning
data.value: • "USB debugging" greyed out or phone not detected: turn off "Auto Blocker" (Settings › Security and privacy), then "Block USB connections". • Secure Folder: unlock it before launching, or the game is not found there.

data.name: BrandOnePlusWarning
data.value: Also turn on "USB debugging (Security settings)", or mouse and keyboard do nothing, and "Install via USB", in the same menu.

data.name: BrandVivoWarning
data.value: Also turn on "USB debugging (Security settings)", or mouse and keyboard do nothing, and "Install via USB", in the same menu.

data.name: SessionRecovering
data.value: The link to {0} dropped. Reopening its window.

data.name: SessionRecoveryGaveUp
data.value: {0}: link lost, its window will reopen when the phone is back.

data.name: ReducedRender
data.value: {0}: the phone runs the game at {1} % of its resolution (this copy's game mode), hence the blurry picture. The triangle on its line sets it back to standard.

data.name: ReducedRenderTip
data.value: The phone draws this game at a reduced resolution: click to fix

data.name: ReducedRenderHeading
data.value: Image reduced to {0} % by the phone

data.name: ReducedRenderExplain
data.value: This copy's Android game mode (performance, saving…) draws the game smaller, then enlarges it: the picture is blurry. Standard mode draws it at full size.

data.name: RestoreStandardModeNote
data.value: The game restarts: the character is disconnected for a few seconds.

data.name: ReducedRenderManual
data.value: Still blurry? On the phone, in game: game panel (Game Booster on Samsung, Game Turbo on Xiaomi) › this game's performance on Standard, then restart the account.

data.name: GameModeRefused
data.value: {0}: the phone refused to change the game mode. On the phone, in game: game panel (Game Booster on Samsung, Game Turbo on Xiaomi) › this game's performance on Standard, then restart the account.

data.name: GameModeNote
data.value: Applies when the game next starts (restart button). Modes other than standard can make the image blurry.

data.name: QuietReducedRender
data.value: Don't warn when the phone reduces the image

data.name: StopReducedRenderWarning
data.value: Don't warn me again for this account

data.name: StandardDidNotHelp
data.value: The game is in the standard mode and still reduced: the setting is elsewhere on the phone.

data.name: GameLeftRunning
data.value: {0} closed, but the game is still running on the phone: it could not be reached. Close it from the phone.

data.name: ReopenFailed
data.value: {0} could not reopen. Reopen it from the list.

data.name: WaitingPhoneText
data.value: The Wi-Fi link is down. The game comes back here as soon as it resumes.

data.name: GameDiedRestarted
data.value: The game of {0} stopped on the phone: it was restarted in its window.

data.name: GameDiedAgain
data.value: The game of {0} stopped on the phone again. Restart it with the looping arrow on its row, in the panel.

data.name: DeviceBatteryLow
data.value: The phone is down to {0} % and is not charging. Plug it in, or the session will end before you do.

data.name: DeviceBatteryCritical
data.value: The phone is down to {0} % and is not charging. Plug it in now: it has a few minutes left.

data.name: DeviceStorageLow
data.value: The phone has only {0} GB free. DOFUS Touch can fail without saying why when space runs out.

data.name: DeviceMemoryLow
data.value: The phone's memory is full ({0} GB available): actions may lag. Close the other apps, lower an account's quality or restart the phone.

data.name: DeviceMemoryCritical
data.value: Phone memory nearly exhausted ({0} GB free): Android will close apps, the game included. Close the other apps, lower an account's quality or restart the phone.

data.name: PhoneMemoryStrain
data.value: The phone is overloaded: it is short of memory and keeps freeing some{0}. Restart it and close the apps running in the background.

data.name: PhoneGameHeavy
data.value: DOFUS Touch takes {0} % of the phone's processor: lower the graphics in the game's options or set the quality to Low.

data.name: PhoneBusy
data.value: The phone's processor is saturated by other apps{0}: close them or restart the phone.

data.name: PhoneWifiSpikes
data.value: Unstable Wi-Fi: {0} spikes in a minute, up to {1} ms. • Far from the router: move the phone closer. • Already next to it: it is the phone's Wi-Fi sleep, only the USB cable avoids it.

data.name: PcBusy
data.value: The PC is {0} % busy: close heavy programs or set the quality to Low.

data.name: DeviceStorageCritical
data.value: The phone has only {0} GB free. Make room before playing: the game will fail.

data.name: DeviceLinkCrowded
data.value: Crowded Wi-Fi channel: {0} % of frames resent, the picture will stutter. Changing the router's channel, or moving the phone closer, helps most.

data.name: DeviceOn24GHz
data.value: The phone is on the 2.4 GHz band. The picture will stutter more than on 5 GHz; switching bands is the single best change you can make.

data.name: InstanceQualityTip
data.value: This account's quality alone. Lower it for the accounts you are not playing: that much less processor, heat and battery.

data.name: InstanceZoomTip
data.value: This account's distance alone: more or less ground in view, at the same window size.

data.name: InstanceZoomWaitsForReopen
data.value: Applies the next time this window opens

data.name: InstanceSettingsTip
data.value: This account's own quality and distance, if it must differ from the others.

data.name: ExportSettingsTip
data.value: Saves accounts, teams, shortcuts and settings to a file, to take them to another PC.

data.name: ImportSettingsTip
data.value: Replaces every setting with those of a file written by this application.

data.name: ImportSettingsConfirm
data.value: This replaces all your accounts, teams, shortcuts and settings. Continue?

data.name: SettingsImported
data.value: Settings restored. Reopen your windows for everything to apply.

data.name: SettingsFileTooNew
data.value: This file was written by a newer version of DT Hub. Update the application before restoring it, otherwise part of your settings would be lost without saying so.

data.name: SettingsFileForeign
data.value: This file is not a DT Hub settings file.

data.name: SettingsFileUnreadable
data.value: This file could not be read.

data.name: DisplayStaysLocked
data.value: Phone locked: its windows show the lock screen instead of the game, this phone cannot avoid it. Unlock it: the game comes back and stays while a window is open.

data.name: DeviceThrottling
data.value: The device is heating up and is starting to slow itself down. Unplug the charger, close an account or drop one quality step, and it will pick up again.

data.name: DeviceThrottlingSevere
data.value: Phone too hot, heavily throttled. Unplug the charger, close an account or lower the quality: otherwise Android suspends the windows while it cools down.

data.name: DeadInputExplanation
data.value: The picture shows, but clicks and keys do nothing, with no error at all: the phone agrees to show its screen, not to receive your input. It is a separate permission, given on the phone.

data.name: DeadInputTestHelp
data.value: Sends the phone a key that does nothing: its answer tells in a second whether it accepts your clicks.

data.name: DeadInputTestWorks
data.value: The device accepts input simulation. If clicks still do nothing, the cause is below, not here.

data.name: DeadInputTestDenied
data.value: The device refuses input simulation. That is the cause: turn on the setting below, then run the check again.

data.name: DeadInputTestUnknown
data.value: No verdict. The device answered something unexpected, and guessing would be worse than saying nothing.

data.name: DeadInputTestNoDevice
data.value: No device connected. Plug one in or pair it, then run the check again.

data.name: DeadInputSecurityHelp
data.value: The most common cause. In the developer options, turn on "USB debugging (Security settings)". Its description mentions "simulating input via USB debugging".

data.name: DeadInputCable
data.value: The cable has to carry data

data.name: DeadInputCableHelp
data.value: When the phone asks for the connection mode, pick "File transfer", not "Charging": while charging, the picture shows but the rest is refused. No question? Try another cable.

data.name: SimulatedKeyboardTip
data.value: Presents the keyboard to the phone as a plugged-in keyboard, bypassing its virtual keyboard.

data.name: SimulatedKeyboardHelp
data.value: Turn on if the mouse works but nothing gets typed. Then set the Android keyboard layout like the PC's, or an AZERTY types as QWERTY.

data.name: DeadInputRevokeHelp
data.value: Developer options › "Revoke USB debugging authorizations". Unplug, plug back in, then accept the prompt again. Unblocks the cases where everything looks right.

data.name: DeadInputToggleDeveloper
data.value: Turn it all off, restart, turn it all back on

data.name: DeadInputToggleDeveloperHelp
data.value: 1. Unplug the phone. 2. Turn off its debugging switches: USB debugging, install via USB, USB debugging (Security settings). 3. Restart the phone, then turn them back on. 4. Plug it back in as "File transfer" and accept the prompt. The order and the restart matter: without them, the setting stays ticked without applying.

data.name: OnBrandUseClonePath
data.value: On a {0} device, the manual copy goes through: {1}.

data.name: OpenThisPageTip
data.value: Open this page in your usual browser, on the original site

data.name: OpenCurrentPageTip
data.value: Open the current page in your usual browser, on the original site

data.name: TranslateTip
data.value: Opens this page in your browser, translated into the application's language by Google Translate. The site is only written in another language.

data.name: AlmanaxTip
data.value: Today's offering and bonus for DOFUS Touch, read from Ankama's own portal.

data.name: DiscordTip
data.value: Join the DT Hub Discord server: news, questions, help.

data.name: AlmanaxSource
data.value: Official Almanax, krosmoz.com, filtered on DOFUS Touch

data.name: AlmanaxCopyTip
data.value: Copies the item's name. Ctrl+V in the game's marketplace search pastes it.

data.name: AlmanaxPrepareTip
data.value: Reads the next seven days of the official Almanax and lists the offerings to bring.

data.name: AlmanaxSearchHint
data.value: A profession or a bonus, for instance Miner

data.name: AlmanaxSearchTip
data.value: Reads the next two months one day at a time and lists every day whose bonus matches. A profession also brings the days good for all of its kind.

data.name: AlmanaxPickTip
data.value: Pick another date, further ahead or further back

data.name: ActionAlmanaxDetail
data.value: Opens today's offering and bonus for DOFUS Touch, read from Ankama's own portal. The window also lets you look ahead to prepare.

data.name: AlmanaxUnavailable
data.value: The Almanax could not be read. The portal may be unreachable, or its page may have changed.

data.name: SearchOnSiteTip
data.value: Open the site's own search in your browser. It looks inside the articles, so it finds items, monsters and characters that this list does not index.

data.name: SearchTip
data.value: Click to unroll the list, or type a name. Accents do not count.

data.name: QuestSearchPlaceholder
data.value: Search for a quest, an area, an achievement, a dungeon or a path

data.name: BackToPreviousPageTip
data.value: Go back to the page seen before

data.name: PreviousStepTip
data.value: Previous step. The page moves back onto it.

data.name: NextStepTip
data.value: Next step. The page moves onto it.

data.name: ReportErrorTip
data.value: Report an error to papycha.fr on this page. The site's form opens with the area and the quest already noted, and nothing is sent until you press.

data.name: QuestInSuccessTip
data.value: Where this quest sits in its achievement

data.name: PreviousQuestTip
data.value: Go back to the previous quest of the achievement

data.name: NextQuestTip
data.value: Move on to the next quest of the achievement

data.name: ClickQuestsHint
data.value: Click to open those that are quests.

data.name: WindowFreezes
data.value: A window freezes after a while

data.name: SleepExplanation
data.value: Android puts to sleep the apps it thinks are idle, including a game window that is not in front: the windows then freeze one by one. A single setting prevents it, and it holds.

data.name: SettingCalledPrefix
data.value: On this device, the setting to find is called “

data.name: RemoveRestrictions
data.value: 2. Take it out of the restrictions

data.name: RemoveRestrictionsHelp
data.value: The game must be allowed to run in the background without limit. Often the only setting needed, and it survives restarts.

data.name: RepeatForEachCopy
data.value: 3. Do it again for each copy of the game

data.name: RepeatForEachCopyHelp
data.value: Each copy of the game, cloned or in another profile, has its own settings: do it again for each one.

data.name: AlreadyFrozenHelp
data.value: A window that has already frozen is repaired by restarting it: the “Restart” button on its row restarts the game without closing the window.

data.name: HotkeySectionSwitching
data.value: Going from one account to another

data.name: ActionAccountDetail
data.value: Brings forward the account on this line of the list, in its tab when it is housed in the tabbed frame. A locked window counts too.

data.name: ActionToggleSettingsDetail
data.value: Shows or hides this window. Game windows stay open, and their title recalls this shortcut.

data.name: ActionNextWindowDetail
data.value: Goes to the next window, in the list's order. Windows set aside are skipped.

data.name: ActionPreviousWindowDetail
data.value: Goes to the previous window, in the list's order. Windows set aside are skipped.

data.name: ActionStackWindowsDetail
data.value: Stacks every window on the last one used, at its place and size. Locked windows do not move.

data.name: ActionTileDetail
data.value: Lays two windows side by side, each on one half of the screen. The active window goes to the right.

data.name: ActionGridDetail
data.value: Lays the windows out in a grid, each on a quarter of the screen, in the order of the list. Beyond four, the next ones stack on the last cell.

data.name: ActionToggleGuidesDetail
data.value: Shows or hides the papycha.fr guides (quests, dungeons, paths…), which stay above the game windows.

data.name: ActionSize1Detail
data.value: The smallest of the four sizes, adjustable with the slider.

data.name: ActionSize2Detail
data.value: The second of the four sizes, adjustable with the slider.

data.name: ActionSize3Detail
data.value: The third of the four sizes, adjustable with the slider.

data.name: ActionSize4Detail
data.value: The largest of the four sizes: the whole usable screen area, without the taskbar. Not full screen.

data.name: ActionFullscreenDetail
data.value: Borderless full screen. Press again, or Esc, to leave it: while in full screen, Esc no longer reaches the game.

data.name: ActionScreenOffDetail
data.value: Switches off the screen of the game window's phone, or of every phone from another DT Hub window, while the game keeps running. Pressed again, lights it back on.

data.name: TurnScreenOffNowTip
data.value: Switches the phone's screen off, the game keeps running. Ctrl+E does the same.

data.name: TurnScreenOnNowTip
